author: Adam Burke
prose: The American Conference seems pretty wide-open for the 2026 season and it’s fair to wonder if any team will have the record or resume to represent the Group of Six in the College Football Playoff. There are four new head coaches and five second-year head coaches in the conference, so nine of the league’s 14 teams are tough to project. Tenured coaches might have an inside track this season, but anything could happen. In terms of preseason conference winner odds, only the MAC has a higher-priced favorite than the American and seven of the 14 teams are priced at +800 or lower. Navy is the tepid favorite here with one of the more tenured coaches in the conference, as Brian Newberry begins his fourth season at the helm. UTSA’s Jeff Traylor and Army’s Jeff Monken are the only two sideline bosses with more years under their belts than Newberry. It probably isn’t a coincidence that UTSA (+480) and Army (6-1) are the second and third favorites, respectively, behind Navy (+310). Life is tough in the American Conference for college football these days. As mentioned, nine of the 14 teams have head coaches hired within the last two seasons because this conference is a springboard to Power Four jobs. Furthermore, any players that stand out are going to be on the minds of SEC, ACC, Big Ten, and Big 12 teams that are looking to fill some voids and plug some holes. In some respects, the service academies have an advantage in that they aren’t watching players go out the door for NIL paydays, but they also can’t leverage the transfer portal to their advantage. Outside of Army and Navy, just about every program in the conference has fewer than 10 returning starters. But, that doesn’t mean they are immune to big personnel losses, especially in Navy’s case with QB Blake Horvath. In a high-variance conference, there should be money to be made, whether you can isolate overachievers or underachievers with props and futures before the season or on a weekly basis. american

author: Adam Burke
prose: From a College Football Playoff standpoint, the ACC had grown accustomed to leaving the party early until Miami showed up in a big way this past season. Clemson was a major player in the late 2010s, including two National Championships, but their one appearance in the last five seasons was a one-and-done as the No. 12 team in 2024. Florida State had a cameo appearance back in 2014 and relative newcomer SMU, who joined the conference in 2024, had a very short-lived appearance that same season. The Hurricanes were unable to finish the job and lost to Indiana, but Mario Cristobal was able to flip the proverbial bird to the doubters and haters with wins over Texas A&M, Ohio State, and Ole Miss before the 27-21 loss to the Hoosiers. The question now is whether or not Miami can piggyback off of that success. Because if they can’t, it looks like another season in which the ACC will be represented in the CFP simply by virtue of being a major conference with an automatic bid and having a seat at the table tall enough to get a team in the field. Incredibly, Miami didn’t even play in the ACC Championship Game last season, as that was between Duke and Virginia. The Blue Devils upset the Cavaliers, which kept Virginia out of the CFP. In the end, it worked out and the conference’s best team made the biggest statement in December and January. Despite some extremely heavy personnel losses, especially on defense, the Hurricanes (-136) still seem to have the inside track in the conference as a very clear odds-on favorite to celebrate in Charlotte on December 5. With SMU (7-1) and Louisville (8-1) as the only other teams lined in single digits to win the ACC at time of publish, it sure looks like the door is open for somebody to step up and challenge Miami. After all, five teams went 6-2 in conference play and five more went 4-4 last season. I’ll be nice and call it parity. Really, this just isn’t a very good conference top to bottom. ACC

author: Zach Cohen
prose: Texas Tech stole the headlines in the Big 12 last season, winning the league and grabbing an automatic College Football Playoff berth. The Red Raiders did flame out in the postseason, losing 23-0 to Oregon in the quarterfinals. However, Joey McGuire’s program officially made its presence felt on the national stage. We also saw a tremendous season out of conference runner-up BYU, we witnessed Utah and Houston win double-digit games, and the depth of the league was impressive with nine teams finishing with winning records. Heading into the 2026 season, the Red Raiders are once again expected to finish on top. However, Texas Tech will have to do it without Brendan Sorsby, who was supposed to take the passing game to another level before a gambling scandal derailed everything. The Red Raiders will now need to fight off some much-improved teams without an elite signal-caller. Texas Tech is an odds-on favorite to win the Big 12 Conference Championship, but BYU and Utah aren’t too far back on the oddsboard. Kansas State, Houston, and Arizona are also shorter than 20-1 at DraftKings Sportsbook, and it’d be foolish to rule out 2024 conference champion Arizona State. This simply should be a fascinating year in what has become one of the most interesting leagues in college football. big 12

author: Wes Reynolds
prose: The Big Ten is aiming for its fourth consecutive CFP National Championship here in 2026. In 2023, Michigan won its first national title since 1997 before Jim Harbaugh left his alma mater and took his NCAA show-cause penalty to return to coaching in the NFL. In 2024, the Wolverines’ archrival Ohio State, led by the most talented roster in college football, removed the critics from Ryan Day’s back and won its first national title since 2014. Well, the Big Ten “three-peated” last season. So, was it Ohio State again? Michigan? Penn State? Oregon? USC? No, it was the Indiana Hoosiers going 16-0 and becoming the first FBS team since Yale in 1894 to go 16-0. Curt Cignetti and his Hoosiers also won their first outright Big Ten Championship since 1945. Indiana’s rise to national prominence not only included these championships but was also home to its first Heisman Trophy Winner Fernando Mendoza. Indiana (+250) will attempt to defend with heavy retention on the offensive line and defense to go along with a portal overhaul that includes TCU transfer QB Josh Hoover to replace Mendoza. Ohio State (+180), defeated by the Hoosiers in the Big Ten Championship Game, returns QB Julian Sayin and WR Jeremiah Smith as perhaps the best QB-WR tandem in college football. Oregon (+260), who lost to the Hoosiers twice, brings back 14 starters including QB Dante Moore and arguably the nation’s best defensive line. Those three teams will be consensus top five nationally to start the season, but USC (14-1) is looking to get to the top of the Big Ten for the first time with a defense led by former TCU coach Gary Patterson, who was lured out of retirement. Four programs have new coaches including Michigan (15-1), who brings in Kyle Whittingham from Utah to restore its tarnished image from the Harbaugh recruiting violations and the Sherrone Moore scandal; Michigan State (500-1), who turns to former Northwestern head coach Pat Fitzgerald; Penn State (20-1), who brings in Matt Campbell from Iowa State to win the big ones that James Franklin seemingly never could; UCLA (160-1), who figured that if Indiana can hire a successful head coach from James Madison, then why not do the same with Bob Chesney? big TEN

author: Adam Burke
prose: Recently, Conference USA has been the proving ground for teams moving up from the FCS ranks to the FBS world. This season, that is not the case, as the new teams are in the Mountain West and MAC. However, with Louisiana Tech off to the Sun Belt and UTEP to the Mountain West, Conference USA goes from 12 teams down to 10. This is absolutely the weakest conference in college football. There were 136 FBS teams last season. Jeff Sagarin’s end- of-season rankings had four teams in the conference 158th or lower. Four other teams were ranked 120th or lower. Ironically, the top two teams as ranked by Sagarin - Western Kentucky and Louisiana Tech - weren’t even involved in the conference championship game. Kennesaw State won 19-15 over Jacksonville State in that one. It was a truly impressive season for Kennesaw State. The Owls fired their longtime head coach during their first season as a FBS member in 2024 and hired Jerry Mack, who was a running backs coach in the NFL the season prior and had only been a head coach at NC Central in the mid-2010s. With that win, the Owls avenged their only conference regular-season loss and then got pumped by Western Michigan in the Myrtle Beach Bowl. The Gamecocks may be able to avenge that title game loss, as they look to be a contender once again behind second-year head coach Charles Kelly, as the team lost head coach Rich Rodriguez, had very few returning starters, and still went 7-1 in league action before the loss in the title game. Arguably the biggest storyline of the season is whether or not Liberty will bounce back. After a 21-5 start, including a College Football Playoff appearance, it all fell apart for Jamey Chadwell, as the Flames went just 4-8 last season. Liberty (+260) is the conference favorite over Western Kentucky (+280), who has the longest-tenured coach in the conference as Tyson Helton starts his eighth season. With Jacksonville State (+450) and Delaware (7-1) as the others lined in single digits, this looks to be a wide-open Group of Six conference again. conference usa

author: Adam Burke
prose: Notre Dame and UConn are on two very different paths this season. With the new College Football Playoff qualification and seeding rules, all the Fighting Irish have to do is finish in the top 12 in the CFP rankings and they will automatically be in the field. Based on how good Notre Dame looks this season, it would be a major upset if they aren’t in the field. In fact, DraftKings had the Fighting Irish at -800 to Make the CFP and the ‘No’ was 5-1 for anybody brave enough to take that chance. While UConn never has CFP aspirations, the Huskies were at least worthy of being mentioned in the same breath as the Fighting Irish with back-to-back 9-4 seasons. Unfortunately, it does look like the tide will turn in Storrs, at least to some degree, with Jim Mora Jr. now at Colorado State. Many believe that Jason Candle is a good hire, but he’s had a knack for losing games as a favorite over the course of his career at Toledo and the Huskies have basically nobody back from last season’s team. The story is different in South Bend. While star RBs Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price are now in the NFL, QB CJ Carr is among the Heisman favorites and the defense is chock full of returning production. After missing out on the CFP last season and after losing to Ohio State in the CFP Championship the previous season, there may not be a more motivated team than the Fighting Irish and the schedule has absolutely softened up after last season’s early losses to Miami and Texas A&M proved too much to overcome in the rankings.

author: Adam Burke
prose: The Mid-American Conference performed a one-for-one swap this offseason, shipping off Northern Illinois to the Mountain West and acquiring Sacramento State from the Big Sky Conference at the FCS level. If you don’t understand that trade from a geographic standpoint, neither do I, but the Hornets signed a five-year deal to be a football-only MAC member, as the basketball team will play in the Big West. With UMass rejoining the MAC last season, the conference has 13 teams, with three in Michigan, one in New York, six in Ohio, one in Indiana, one in Massachusetts, and then one in California. As usual, realignment remains a head-scratcher, but we sure have some fascinating travel spots for this season as a result, especially when we get to MACtion in late October and early November with weeknight games. On the whole, the conference isn’t very strong again, but somebody will have to win it. UMass went 0-12 and 0-8 in conference play at one extreme, while Western Michigan went 10-4, including a 7-1 record against MAC opponents. The Broncos put an exclamation point on their season with a 10-point win over Miami (OH) in Detroit for the MAC Championship and a slaughter of Kennesaw State in the Myrtle Beach Bowl. WMU (+360) is co-favored to run it back and their company is Miami, so we could be looking at our first MAC Championship Game rematch since Northern Illinois and Bowling Green played three straight title games from 2013-15. The Falcons (16-1) may not be much of a factor, but their archrival Toledo (4-1) is getting some market love, even with former head coach Jason Candle at UConn. Ohio (+650) and Central Michigan (+750) round out the single-digit shots in what looks like a wide-open conference again. Three teams tied for second at 6-2 last season and there was a battle until the end in 2024 with two teams at 7-1 and two at 6-2. It usually comes down to the last week to see who will represent the conference at Ford Field and this season looks to follow that same path. mac

author: Jonathan Von Tobel
prose: They say success is the greatest revenge, but in this case of jilted lovers, the Mountain West might have some trouble making the defectors to the new Pac-12 jealous. Gone are Boise State, San Diego State, Fresno State, Colorado State and Utah State. To replace them, the conference brought in UTEP, Northern Illinois and North Dakota State. The Bison have a shot to be the hot new fling, but the Miners and Huskies are projected to be cellar-dwellars in their first seasons in the conference. The aforementioned North Dakota State program — which dominated the FCS and the Missouri Valley Football Conference — is one of the short shots to win the Mountain West. UNLV and New Mexico are either tied as favorites or have slight variance in their prices to win it all, depending on the shop. All three programs have rightful claims to their status as true contenders, but the conference does go slightly deeper than that. Hawaii returns quarterback Micah Alejado, who was named preseason Offensive Player of the Year. Timmy Chang has improved his win total each season on the island and has both an effective offense and a favorable schedule in conference play. There is no doubt the Rainbow Warriors are a dark horse of sorts to win the Mountain West. Then there is Troy Calhoun and Air Force. The Falcons won nine games over the last two seasons, but Calhoun has an experienced roster, including quarterback Liam Szarka, who led one of the most efficient offenses in the country last season. Air Force could absolutely find a way to the table of contenders by season’s end. Heartbreak usually leads to change. People hit the gym, change their diets and generally try to improve themselves when they get out of a long-term relationship. The Mountain West certainly tried to do that with the additions it made, but it’s unlikely those that departed for the Pac-12 are amazed by the changes to the conference. Either way, this should be a raucous and volatile season in the Mountain West, and that is great for bettors. mountain west

author: Matt Youmans
prose: It’s football season, yet the unveiling of a new-look Pac-12 Conference brings back memories of the late, great Bill Walton. The basketball legend and colorful broadcaster constantly touted the “conference of champions” due to the league’s impressive history of NCAA titles. Unfortunately, the schools responsible for almost all of those titles — Stanford, UCLA, USC, Cal, Oregon, Washington, Arizona and Arizona State — are long gone and spread to different conferences all over the map. Oregon State and Washington State, the league’s two leftovers, have been joined by a handful of newcomers from the Mountain West (Boise State, San Diego State, Colorado State, Fresno State and Utah State) and a straggler from the Sun Belt (Texas State). The Pac-12 consists of only eight teams and all include the name “State.” The conference will not get an automatic qualifier into the College Football Playoff. Boise State, which won the last three Mountain West championships, is listed by DraftKings as the +170 favorite to win the Pac-12. The Broncos could boast the conference’s top quarterback, Maddux Madsen, and top running back, Dylan Riley. San Diego State, the +370 second choice, went 9-4 last season and is led by workhorse running back Lucky Sutton. The league does present a few intriguing teams beyond the Broncos and Aztecs. In his first season at Fresno State, coach Matt Entz won nine games. Watch out for Entz and the Bulldogs, and keep an eye on Colorado State with new coach Jim Mora Jr., who worked an incredible turnaround at UConn. Texas State arrives with quarterback Brad Jackson triggering an explosive passing attack. The Pac-12 can make a statement, for better or worse, when Boise State opens its season at Oregon on Sept. 5. On the same day, Fresno State visits USC and Washington State plays at Washington. Other nonconference matchups to circle are San Diego State at UCLA (Sept. 12) and BYU at Colorado State (Sept. 19). In the biggest league games, Fresno hosts Boise on Oct. 10 and Boise hosts San Diego State on Nov. 21. pac-12

author: Jonathan Von Tobel
prose: The time at the top of the country has seemingly come to an end for the SEC. It has been three years since a member of the conference won a national championship. The Big Ten has dominated the last three seasons, all with different champions. The conversation all offseason has been about the SEC reclaiming its throne, and there is certainly a strong chance the conference can do just that with its depth of championship contenders. Georgia — the last SEC team to win it all — looks primed to grab its third title of the Kirby Smart era. The Bulldogs have a Heisman Trophy contender in quarterback Gunner Stockton and one of the most experienced rosters in the country. Texas has the experience as well, and the blue-chip prospect at quarterback in Arch Manning. Steve Sarkisian has some CFP wins under his belt and is dying to add to that this season. Given the additions the Longhorns made in the portal, as well as the returning production throughout the roster, the market believes this team is a true contender. Then, you get to some of the dark-horse contenders for both a conference title and national championship. Alabama and Texas A&M both made the CFP last season, but shared similar fates in being dispatched by the eventual participants in the national championship game. The Crimson Tide will have to work in a new quarterback, but they do have a talented roster with a great defense. So too do the Aggies. The difference between the two is the experience Marcel Reed has at quarterback. Let’s not forget Ole Miss, which finished a drive short of a berth in the final, or Oklahoma, which returns most of the best defense in the country. The expectations for the SEC are always a national championship. This year is no different, and the conference boasts many potential contenders. The depth of the conference in terms of quality is not on par with the Big Ten, but no one will be shocked if a program from this conference is hoisting a trophy come January. sec

author: Adam Burke
prose: The Sun Belt remains the only conference in college football to still use divisions, as the 14 teams in the conference are split right down the middle to form the East and West. Traditionally, the East has been stronger with teams like App State and Coastal Carolina and only got stronger when James Madison and Marshall joined the conference. The West is headlined primarily by Louisiana and Troy, but Louisiana Tech is a conference newcomer this season looking to make some noise. Texas State jumped ship to join the reimagined Pac-12. Conference favorite James Madison has experienced big changes once again, as Bob Chesney followed predecessor Curt Cignetti to the Big Ten. Billy Napier, lovingly (sort of) referred to as “Sun Belt Billy” for his time at Louisiana, is back in the conference now after falling short of expectations at Florida. Incredibly, he is one of just three new head coaches in the conference, as we usually see a lot of turnover in the Sun Belt and similar leagues. The others are Ryan Beard at Coastal Carolina and Blake Anderson, another former Sun Belt boss, at Southern Miss. This is a conference that is important to know because of the early-season weeknight games across the ESPN family of networks, so you’re going to get a few standalone Sun Belt nights where those teams are front and center before we really get into the NBA and NHL seasons. There can be some excellent betting opportunities for those who are keeping tabs on the conference. Of course, the carrot of the College Football Playoff berth that dangles in front of the highest-ranked G6 conference champ is something that adds intrigue to the season. Last year, it was James Madison who locked that up and put forth a decent effort against Oregon, covering the 21-point number in a 17-point loss. The Dukes are +270 to run it back in the “Fun Belt”, but they are +1500 to make the CFP for a second straight year. Old Dominion is the second shot at +460 before we get to Louisiana (7-1) and Troy (8-1), so the East looks to be outpacing the West yet again. sun belt
